title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
gist: Solid-state transformers combine silicon-carbide power electronics with small magnetic cores and are emerging as a data-center-first answer to the transformer shortage. A 1 MW NC State prototype reached about 98% efficiency against about 96% for conventional equipment, and Heron Power raised $140M and is building a 40 GW/year factory. High-voltage transmission units remain out of reach while wait times for large conventional transformers stretch to five years.

insights.claim: Wait times for large conventional transformers, the kind needed to connect new power plants, long-distance transmission and data centers, are stretching as long as five years.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Boucher
insights.so_what: Transformer lead times limit how fast data center and generation capacity can come online, giving pricing power to equipment makers.
insights.quote: “Transformers have become one of the biggest bottlenecks for utilities, generation developers, and even data centers,”

insights.claim: Grid equipment makers have invested $1.7 billion in the US supply chain for power transformers and another $1.3 billion for distribution transformers, but this still is not keeping pace with grid growth.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Boucher
insights.so_what: About $3B in new capacity is still too little, so the shortage and premium pricing are likely to last.

insights.claim: Transformer manufacturing is hard to scale because it is technical and needs a lot of specialized labor, so even factories announced years ago are still years from opening.
insights.speaker: Benjamin Boucher
insights.so_what: Supply cannot respond quickly to demand, which favours incumbents with existing plants and alternative technologies.
insights.quote: “Without the transformers, you don’t really have an electrical grid.”

insights.claim: Solid-state transformers convert AC to DC and then to high-frequency AC with silicon carbide switches, which lets the magnetic core shrink dramatically; some reach roughly one-tenth the size of conventional units at the same capacity.
insights.speaker: Srdjan Lukic
insights.so_what: Growth in solid-state transformers would add demand for silicon carbide power semiconductors and reduce dependence on electrical steel and copper.

insights.claim: Solid-state transformers take over the jobs of rectifiers and inverters, shrinking the total footprint of electrical equipment and potentially cutting system power losses.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Replacing several devices with one threatens the separate markets for inverters and rectifiers.

insights.claim: A one-megawatt solid-state transformer built in Lukic's lab and tested by the New York Power Authority and EPRI was roughly 98% efficient, against about 96% for an equivalent conventional transformer plus rectifier, halving power losses.
insights.speaker: Srdjan Lukic
insights.so_what: Halving conversion losses is a meaningful saving at data center scale.

insights.claim: The tested prototype runs at only about 15,000 volts, while larger data centers need higher-voltage connections and transmission lines run at hundreds of thousands of volts, so high-voltage solid-state units need new materials and designs.
insights.speaker: Srdjan Lukic
insights.so_what: Solid-state transformers will not ease the shortage of large transmission transformers any time soon.

insights.claim: Power electronics give solid-state transformers more failure modes than conventional units. Heron counters with a modular design of many small units, so one failure does not take the whole system offline.
insights.speaker: Drew Baglino
insights.so_what: Reliability is the main adoption risk, and a modular design is the main way to reduce it.

insights.claim: Companies developing solid-state transformers are mostly targeting data centers now, because money is pouring in and the voltages needed are lower than for long-distance transmission.
insights.speaker: Srdjan Lukic
insights.so_what: AI data center capex is funding the commercialization of new grid technology.

insights.claim: Heron Power raised $140 million in February to commercialize its Heron Link solid-state transformer for data centers, solar arrays and grid batteries, with 10 MWh of battery testing and a solar farm pilot planned.
insights.speaker: Drew Baglino
insights.so_what: A well-funded early mover in a supply-constrained market.

insights.claim: Heron Power is building a $100 million California factory that should begin production in 2027 and reach a full rate of 40 gigawatts of transformers per year in 2029.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: 40 GW a year would be meaningful capacity; watch whether the ramp stays on schedule.
